Morgan Stanley Interview
Experience
Utsav Khatu | T.Y.B.Tech 2019-23
06th September 2021
OVERVIEW
Morgan Stanley , an American multinational investment bank and financial services
company visited our campus for Internships for 3rd Year Students. Morgan Stanley
offered 2 Tracks for Internship . And Around 200+ Students Applied for the Internship.
Eligibility Criteria was :
●
Circuital Branch Students
●
CGPA 7.5+
Two Tracks were :
●
App Dev Track :
●
Enterprise Engineering Track
PS : I had Selected App Dev Track. (Please Remember , throughout the Exp. App Dev
Track’s Details are mentioned)
Also Last Year (2020) only App Dev Track was offered , So it might vary for you.
Round 1 : Online Test ( 3rd Sept , 1hrs 40mins)
Online Test was conducted on the AMCAT Platform. There were three different sections.
●
Aptitude Section (20 mins) :
○
General Mathematical Questions were asked (Around 11th , 12th level)
mainly consisting of topics like : Permutation & Combination , Profit & Loss
, Seating Arrangements  and Statistics. Most of them are easy but due to
time constraints , most students are not able to solve all of them.
1

○
They were 10 question out of which i was able to solve 8 of them
○
Most of the questions were formula based so you could refer this :
https://www.indiastudychannel.com/resources/78963-List-of-Formulas-usef
●
Debugging Section (20 mins):
○
There was a option to choose your Java , C++ and Python
○
This Section involved 7 easy debugging questions.
○
I was able to solve all of them except for one where only 4/6 Test Cases
Worked
●
Coding Section (60 mins)
○
This Section contained 3 Questions . All of them were pretty standard ones
Q1 : Find the length of the longest valid substring.
Ex  )()() , here the answer is 4.
Made a silly mistake over here so only 11 out of 12 TC passed.
Q2 : Given a pair of numbers denoting the starting and ending of the search
region over which an object is requested. There are 1-n objects passed in the
linear format and you were asked to find the minimum distance travelled by a
single robot to search the regions such that the search region of the robots do not
overlap.
Ex: Given n = 10 and the pairs of numbers : 1 5 , 6 7, 7 8. Here we require 2 robots
searching the 2 regions, one from 1 to 5 and around from 6 to 8 (since the last to
overlap) . So the answer would be 3 (i.e 6->8 = 8-6+1) .
I was able to pass 15 out of 16 TC  . The question was based upon this :
Overlapping Merge Intervals
Q3 :  Given ‘n’ objects (numbered from 0 to n-1) for each ‘m’ different category
(numbered from 0 to m-1) of price Pij where i denotes the ith element and j
denotes the jth category  , you need to choose the minimum n elements numbered
from 0 to n-1 such that no 2 adjacent element has same category. Ie for ‘1’ you
have chosen the 2th category , for ‘0’ and ‘2’ you can’t choose the 2th category. This
was a DP Problem and I was able to pass 13 out of 14 TC.
This Concluded Round 1 and results were declared in the evening on the same day.
2

25 Students were selected for App Dev Track and 13 Students were selected for EE
Track.
Round 2 : Technical Round (1 hr 15 min)
This Round varies from student to student , Be Prepared for questions based on OS,
DBMS, OOPs , Your Main Programming Lang. (mine was c++) , Low Level Design using
OOP and Database Design using SQL Queries.
So for the Round was as below :
●
Introduce yourself (Now this is the most important part because what you say
here could be cross questioned from Interviewer like why did you choose this
project ? , Why did you choose this Tech Stack , Other Project Specific Questions ,
etc ) . So be prepared for it.
●
Next was the Questions based on my Resume i.e the Work Exp, Project and Project
Specific Question . The above 2 lasted around (15 mins)
●
Then I was asked to solve a DSA Problem : Interleave the Linked List from front to
end. Ex : Let the linked list be 1->2->3->4->5 so the answer would be 1->5->2->4->3.
He also gave the constraints which were Time Complexity Should be O(n) and
Space Complexity Should be O(1) (Now this was a rare case where interviewer
gave away the Constraints in the beginning itself ) Usually One should start with
clearing the Question and should jump to assumptions of your’s then present a
Naive Approach and then he/she slowly and slowly optimize it and it shows your
Thought Process. I presented him 2 Approaches : recursive one and another using
the reversal of the latter half. He asked me to DRY RUN the code and also
discussed the Time and Space Complexity of the 2 Approaches (20 mins)
●
After this part he discussed more about the Work Exp. Project and fews OS
concept’s real word questions were asked. (10mins)
●
Then I was asked to implement the Work Exp Project using Low Level Design
Concepts using OOPS. He wanted a rough overview of what the classes would be ,
the relation between them and the functionalities of them. Here the code which i
wrote wasn’t satisfactory so instead i manipulated the flow of Discussion to OOPS
& C++  by calling out the topics from OOPS & C++ in the code explanation . This
worked and he asked me about the virtual function, pure virtual functions ,
abstract classes , etc (PS: What i did may not in every interview ) (20mins)
●
Overall He seemed satisfied with answers and asked me if I had any questions.
3

(Do Ask Question , because it shows your interests in the Company and the Job
Post). This lasted around 10 mins .
Total of 16 people were selected for the next round (4 from EE and 12 from APP DEV)
and fortunately I was one of them.
Round 3 : Professional Fitness Round (1hr)
●
I was expecting a Technical + Professional Fitness Round but it turned out to be
just a Professional Fitness Round.
●
I was prepared for HR Questions for this round but except for the Intro , none of
them were asked (Be Prepared tho , some of them were asked the typical HR
Questions).
●
Most of the Questions asked here were to judge your personality , thinking and
behaviour .
●
Some Opinion and Situation based questions were asked too.
●
Some of the Questions asked in the interview (which i could remember) were :
○
How much of a risk taking person you are ?
○
How do you see yourself ?
○
Would you lead others or are willing to follow others ?
○
Suppose you are not comfortable with working with a person or that
person not working according to what you want , how would you behave in
this situation ? Did this happen before ?
Most of the questions didn’t require any preparation but recollection of your past
journey would be a nice option , because if you can co-relate the question asked in the
interview to the real life situation which has occurred before , there are decent chances
of yours of getting selected.
Total of 11 Students were selected for the Internship (2 from the EE and 9 from APP DEV
Track) and the Result was announced on the same day itself. And I was fortunate to be
one of them.
Tips :
●
For the Preparation  you could use the following :
4

○
For Problem Solving try few Competitive Problems
○
For Data Structure & Algorithm you could go with 450dsa (recommended) or
striver’s list
○
For OS understand the concepts behind the topic . You can learn the concept
from GateSmashers OS Playlist and the theory from here
○
For DBMS again understand the concept behind the topic using Sanchit Jain’s
Playlist and the theory from here
○
For OOP Concepts you can try this
○
For Low Level System Design , learn it from Soumyajit Bhattacharya’s
Playlist
○
For SQL Queries refer TutorialsPoint and practice on HackerRank
○
For DataBase Design , i just read through the previous DataBase Design
questions
○
This should be enough for the internship drive and it can be completed within
2-3 months
●
Don’t lose your cool during the process. Stay hydrated and optimistic
●
Be Confident while answering the question a lot of weightage is on it
●
Explain every process of your thought while solving the problem
●
Do not lie on your resume or try to cheat on the interview. Be honest and have trust
in yourself.
●
Don’t get Dejected by the failure , there will be many opportunities during the
internship drive just keep learning and you will succeed.
All the Best :)
5
